~20% new content that corrects an earlier mistake.

foreignObject.div: Reset-and-extend. The recap restates the entire training loop for new joiners. The new material lands two corrections at once — softmax is the right output for multi-class (not sigmoid + threshold bands), and the hidden-layer activation is independent of the output-layer activation.

svg.text: Look at Y. Pick the output layer.

g.text: Hidden layers in all three cases: ReLU. The hidden-layer activation is independent of the output-layer activation.

svg.text: Three classes, real numbers, the bands trick made wrong

g.text: Not sigmoid + threshold bands. The bands have no loss signal, classes have no order, adding a class breaks everything.

svg.text: TF / Keras / PyTorch / JAX — which to use when
Theano (2008–2017): discontinued. Mentioned only because the Keras backends story includes it.
The bridge from theory to code

g.text: # 1. Create a per-project env (don't install into base)
# 3. Install packages into THIS env only
pip install tensorflow keras numpy pandas
# 4. Launch Jupyter (must be inside the activated env)
If your prompt doesn't show (genai) in parens, you forgot conda activate. Stop and retry — half of all “works on my machine” stories trace here.

svg.text: Three rules, three corrections, one forward link

g.text: ① Softmax for multi-class, sigmoid for binary, identity for regression. Output layer is task-specific.
② Hidden-layer activation is ReLU, regardless of what task you're solving.
③ Always conda activate before pip install. Never install into base.
① “John John Hoffer” → John Hopfield (Princeton; 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics with Hinton).
② “Neural networks are black boxes” — substantially out of date in 2026. Mechanistic interpretability is real.
③ “Stop when error = 0” — stop on gradient ≈ 0 or early stopping on validation loss.
The next session is hands-on Keras: image classification with sparse_categorical_crossentropy.
Original recording: ~mid-October 2024 (Hinton + Hopfield Nobel + Dussehra references). See §02 of the notes.
